Not that much. I just ran a benchmark of the same framework action as the one use for the issue report (10k klib). Here are the results

A is with this packageFragment patch and B is without.

```
Usable data from 205/205 runs.

| Measure              | p50      | p90      | p95      |
|----------------------|----------|----------|----------|
| Action A wall time   |   294.84 |   432.46 |   451.81 |
| Action B wall time   |   431.30 |   669.46 |   747.36 |
| Action A CPU time    |   512.10 |   677.11 |   695.66 |
| Action B CPU time    |   636.70 |   917.02 |  1012.21 |
| Action A peak memory | 17.62GiB | 17.68GiB | 17.70GiB |
| Action B peak memory | 17.19GiB | 17.26GiB | 17.28GiB |

Total wall time ratio (B / A): 1.48
Total CPU time ratio (B / A): 1.28
Actions have a significant difference in wall time (p < 0.05).
Action B is slower.
```
Interesting. What does the action include? Is it only the Objective-C header generation, or something more?
This is the full framework it generates the Objective-C header, stubs and bridges
What are the numbers when compiling with `-Xomit-framework-binary`? It basically limits the compilation to generating the header and skips the rest.

Here you go. This is only the `FremeworkHeaderOnly`

A is with this packageFragment patch and B is without.
